stemMd: At the same temperature, replacing saturated fatty-acid tails with cis-unsaturated tails generally has which effect on a phospholipid bilayer?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It makes every tail perfectly straight.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It creates peptide bonds between adjacent lipids.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It converts the bilayer into a protein.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It removes all polar head groups.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It reduces tight packing of the tails.

explanationMd: Cis double bonds introduce bends that hinder close packing. The result generally favours greater membrane fluidity at the same temperature. It is a structural effect of the tails, not replacement of lipid heads.

distractorRationale.c: Lipids remain chemically distinct from proteins.
distractorRationale.d: Unsaturation changes tails, not head groups.
distractorRationale.b: Double bonds are within fatty-acid chains.
